subject: MSA & Order Form — term mechanics, auto-renew, and TFC scenarios
messages:
From: Alex Moran <alex.moran@starlite.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@starlite.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA + Order Form — term mechanics, auto-renew, and TFC redlines

Hi Soojin / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is Starlite's proposed redline to the MSA and a short clean order form PDF. Our legal team is primarily focused on three areas that block internal approval:

1) Auto-renew mechanics — we want a clearer opt-out window and reminder cadence.
2) Notice window — we proposed mutual 60 days for termination for convenience (TFC) and a 120-day ramp for service wind-down.
3) TFC liability cap — we'd like a limited transition credit instead of a full refund mechanism.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate a mutual 60-day notice and a capped TFC (proposed: 25% of remaining commitment) or whether you need to hold to the existing opt-out structure in your MSA? We can be flexible on timing if we get a clear dev/test migration commitment.

Attachments: Starlite_Redline_MSA.docx (tracked), OrderForm_Draft.pdf

Appreciate a quick read — procurement is aiming to circulate the package to finance by EOD Monday.

Best,
Alex
Head of Procurement, Starlite AI

[Attachment: OrderForm_Draft.pdf (pdf, 48KB)]

Alex — thanks for sending these over and for the clear ask. We want to move fast on this so Starlite can get finance approval. Quick notes while I loop in Legal and RevOps: 

- We can run a short "exit simulation" to model the cost/operational impact of a 60-day mutual notice + 120-day wind-down. Naomi, can you load the attached exit-simulations.xlsx and run against the current order form volumes? Please include token cost delta and engineering handover hours.
- Ben, I'd like Legal to propose two fallback language options: (A) mutual 60-day notice with a capped TFC credit (Starlite's ask), and (B) Redwood's preferred approach (standard auto-renew with a 30–90 day opt-out window). We want to present both to Starlite with clear tradeoffs.

If we can get those materials by EOD Monday, I'll package a short decision memo and propose a 30-minute sync with Alex and procurement Tue morning.

Attachments: exit-simulations.xlsx (blank template)

Thanks —
Sooj

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T16:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — term mechanics, auto-renew, and TFC redlines

Sooj / Naomi — I reviewed Starlite's tracked changes and sketched comments in the attached file. High level:

- Mutual 60-day notice is defensible but increases operational risk for certain reserved-capacity commitments. If Starlite insists, we should pair it with either (i) a limited transition SLA that preserves their traffic for 60 days but reduces burst/priority for 120 days, or (ii) an early-termination credit capped at 25% of remaining committed fees (their proposed number).
- Auto-renew: propose we keep a 1-year renewal cadence but agree to a 30–60 day reminder and a 30-day opt-out window immediately prior to renewal (this is a compromise on our standard 30-day opt-out).
- TFC language: prefer a simple credit approach rather than complex escrow/refund mechanisms. If we offer a credit, we should specify permitted use (e.g., one-time credit applied to transition services or final invoice).

I attached redline_comments.docx with tracked comments and two inserted paragraph options for the MSA: Option A (mutual 60-day + 25% capped credit) and Option B (standard auto-renew with expanded reminder cadence). We should surface the options to Starlite with an explicit operational impact table.

Naomi — can you run the exit-sim spreadsheet and add an "operational risk" column (low/medium/high) and estimated engineering hours to close? I'll add legal risk notes after that.

Date: 2026-10-09T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — term mechanics, auto-renew, and TFC scenarios (next steps)

Alex — thanks for the patience. Quick update and proposed next steps: 

1) Attached summary for Starlite: two discrete options (Option A = mutual 60-day + 25% capped TFC credit, Option B = Redwood standard with enhanced reminders and a 30-day opt-out prior to renewal). I also included an operational impact annex.
2) Naomi ran the exit simulations and attached a short risk + hours summary — bottom line: mutual 60-day increases handover work by ~40% in peak months but is manageable if Starlite signs a 60-day migration plan (we can share the template).
3) Ben will send a clean tracked MSA with the two paragraph options; Legal prefers the capped credit wording for clarity.

Proposed meeting: Tue 2026-10-12 09:00 PT (30 min) to pick Option A or B and agree on order form language. If Starlite picks Option A, we will include a one-time transition credit equal to 25% of remaining committed fees, applied as a credit on the final invoice, and a 60-day migration plan template in Schedule 3.

If that works, I'll share a short decision memo and a DocuSign packet by EOD Monday.

Next actions for Alex: confirm Tue 10/12 09:00 PT or propose another time.

Thanks —
Sooj
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Counsel, Redwood Inference
